We need to solve the geometric optics problem: 120 lenses, starting with object 30 cm to left of lens 1. Use thin lens equation 1/s + 1/s' = 1/f. For each lens, object distance s (positive if object left of lens), image distance s' (positive if image right). Then the image becomes object for next lens, with object distance = distance between lenses minus s' (if s' positive, object is to left of next lens, so s_next = d - s'? Actually careful: The image from lens i is located at distance s'_i from lens i. The distance from lens i to lens i+1 is d_i (given). Then the object for lens i+1 is that image. If s'_i is positive (real image to right of lens i), then the object for lens i+1 is to the left if s'_i < d_i, because the image is before the next lens. Then object distance for lens i+1 is d_i - s'_i (positive). If s'_i > d_i, then the image is beyond the next lens, so the light converges to a point behind lens i+1, which means the object for lens i+1 is virtual (to the right), so s_{i+1} = d_i - s'_i (negative). If s'_i is negative (virtual image to left of lens i), then the image is on the left side, so for lens i+1, the object is to the left? Actually if the image is virtual, it is on the same side as the object. The light diverges from that virtual image. For lens i+1, that virtual image acts as a real object if it is to the left of lens i+1? Wait: A virtual image from lens i is formed by diverging rays that appear to come from a point on the left side. Those rays then go to lens i+1. The rays are diverging from that point. So for lens i+1, that point is a real object if it is to the left of lens i+1. So if s'_i is negative, the virtual image is at distance |s'_i| to the left of lens i. Then its distance to lens i+1 is d_i + |s'_i| = d_i - s'_i (since s'_i negative). That's positive, so object distance positive (real object). So the general formula: s_{i+1} = d_i - s'_i. That's correct, because if s'_i is positive (real image to right), then s_{i+1} can be positive or negative; if s'_i negative (virtual image left), then d_i - s'_i > d_i > 0, so always positive. So we can iterate.
